verse.speaker: Arjuna
verse.setting: Arjuna confesses the mind is as hard to hold as the wind; Krishna answers.
verse.sanskrit: चञ्चलं हि मनः कृष्ण प्रमाथि बलवद्दृढम् । तस्याहं निग्रहं मन्ये वायोरिव सुदुष्करम् ॥
verse.line: The mind is restless, stormy, stubborn and strong. Holding it feels like holding the wind.
verse.translation: For the mind is restless, Krishna, turbulent, powerful and stubborn. I think it is as hard to hold as the wind.
verse.why: The mind is hard to hold, but practice and letting go train it.

prasang.title: Mastering the mind
prasang.summary: Arjuna says the mind is restless, stormy and stubborn. Krishna agrees, and says practice and letting go can train it.
prasang.lesson: The mind is hard to hold, but practice and letting go train it.

verse.meaning: Arjuna stands before Krishna and admits that the mind is restless, stormy, powerful, and stubborn. He says it feels as hard to hold as the wind. Krishna agrees. He tells Arjuna that practice and letting go will train it. The mind is not meant to be caged, but to be steadied through repeated, gentle effort.
verse.for_you: You are at two in the morning, replaying the same messages. The visa is real, and the fear is real. But the mind at this hour is not solving the problem. It is only exhausting you. Let the replaying rest.

verse.speaker: Janaka
verse.setting: Janaka, having chosen to keep ruling, talks gently to his own restless mind at night.
verse.sanskrit: यथा यथा विकल्पौघान्संकल्पयसि हेलया । तथा तथैति स्फारत्वं संसारस्तव चिन्तया ॥
verse.line: The more scenarios you spin, the bigger your world of worry grows.
verse.translation: The more you casually spin up fancies and possibilities, the more your world of troubles swells, through your own worrying.
verse.why: You don't have to leave your life to change it. Do the day's work with a mind that doesn't clutch.

prasang.title: King Janaka overhears the sages and keeps ruling, with a free mind
prasang.summary: Walking in his spring garden, King Janaka overhears hidden sages singing about the self. Shaken, he climbs to his palace roof and questions everything he has lived for. When his doorkeeper calls him to the day's work, he decides not to run away: he gets up and does his duties, but with a mind that no longer clutches.
prasang.story_hook: One spring morning, a king out for a walk overheard a song that he could not stop thinking about.
prasang.lesson: You don't have to leave your life to change it. Do the day's work with a mind that doesn't clutch.

verse.meaning: King Janaka stands on his palace roof at night, having just heard sages sing that his whole life was a dream. His mind is spinning with questions about duty and truth. He does not leave his kingdom to find the answer. He goes down and rules again, but with a mind that no longer clutches. He tells his own mind that the more it spins up fancies and possibilities, the more its world of troubles swells through its own worrying.
verse.for_you: The visa and the work messages are real, but the 2am replay is a story your mind is telling itself. Let the mind spin for a moment, then set it down. The work will be there in the morning.

verse.speaker: Sugriva
verse.setting: Sugriva, who has lost his own wife and kingdom, steadies a grieving Ram.
verse.sanskrit: व्यसने वार्थकृच्छ्रे वा भये वा जीवितान्तगे। विमृशंश्च स्वया बुद्ध्या धृतिमान् नावसीदति॥
verse.line: In loss, money trouble or fear, the steady person thinks it through and does not go under.
verse.translation: In disaster, in money trouble, in fear, even when life itself is at stake, the steady person who thinks things through with their own mind does not sink.
verse.why: Two people in trouble can carry each other.

prasang.title: Ram and Sugriva's friendship
prasang.summary: Ram and Sugriva swear friendship before a fire. Sugriva shows Ram the jewels Sita dropped; Ram breaks down, and Sugriva comforts him: in trouble the steady person thinks it through, and a friend is the greatest refuge.

verse.meaning: Ram is weeping over Sita. Sugriva, who has lost his wife and kingdom, steps in. He tells Ram that even when everything is falling apart, even when life is on the line, the person who stays steady and thinks clearly will not drown. The verse says that two people in trouble can carry each other, and a friend is the greatest refuge.
verse.for_you: You are carrying a real visa deadline. You are also carrying a mind that checks messages at 2am. This verse says you do not have to sink. You can think it through while you rest.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on how to act without being chained to results.
verse.sanskrit: कर्मण्येवाधिकारस्ते मा फलेषु कदाचन । मा कर्मफलहेतुर्भूर्मा ते सङ्गोऽस्त्वकर्मणि ॥
verse.line: Your work is yours to do; the results are not yours to hold. Don't let that make you stop.
verse.translation: Your right is to the work alone, never to its fruits. Do not let the fruit be your motive, and do not cling to doing nothing.
verse.why: Do the work fully; let go of owning the result.
verse.misuse: This is not 'don't care about results' or 'don't plan'. Care, plan and aim well; just don't let the outcome own you.

prasang.title: The yoga of action
prasang.summary: Krishna teaches the yoga of action: work wholeheartedly, give up clinging to outcomes, stay even in success and failure, and keep a single steady purpose.
prasang.lesson: Do the work fully; let go of owning the result.

verse.meaning: Krishna speaks to Arjuna on the battlefield, right before the war begins. The moment is heavy with duty and doubt, and Arjuna is frozen by what the fight might cost. Krishna tells him to claim his work alone, and to step back from owning what comes after. The verse asks for full effort without the weight of the outcome. It does not ask Arjuna to stop fighting, but to keep his mind steady while the future is still unknown.
verse.for_you: The work you are doing for the visa is real. The result is not. You can hold the effort without holding the fear. Let the checking stop, even for a little while, and let the work stand on its own.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Arjuna asks which devotee is best; Krishna offers a ladder of practices.
verse.line: Practice is good, understanding better, meditation better still. But letting go of results brings peace at once.
verse.translation: Knowledge is better than mere practice; meditation is better than knowledge; giving up the fruit of action is better than meditation. From that renunciation, peace follows immediately.
verse.why: If the ideal is too hard, take the next step down, and keep going.
verse.misuse: Not 'stop caring how things turn out'. Peace comes from releasing the grip, not from indifference.

prasang.title: Form or formless: which devotee is best, and the ways to reach him
prasang.summary: Krishna says devotion to a personal form is easier, then offers a ladder: fix your mind; if not, practise; if not, work for me; if not, let go of results. Letting go brings peace at once.
prasang.lesson: If the ideal is too hard, take the next step down, and keep going.

verse.meaning: Krishna is telling Arjuna that there is a way down the ladder if the top steps feel too steep. If fixing the mind on the divine form is beyond reach, then simply practise. If even that feels heavy, then work for me. And if even that is too much, then take the next step down and let go of the fruit of your actions. That single act of release brings peace immediately, without waiting for the result.
verse.for_you: You have tried to hold the visa outcome with your thoughts, and it has cost you your sleep. Today, you let the rating go for one night. You do what is yours to do, and you let the mind rest, knowing peace follows the release.

verse.speaker: Bhartrihari
verse.sanskrit: परिभ्रमसि किं मुधा क्वचन चित्त विश्राम्यतां स्वयं भवति यद्यथा भवति तत्तथा नान्यथा । अतीतमननुस्मरन्नपि च भाव्यसंकल्पयन् नतर्कितसमागमाननुभवामि भोगानहम् ॥
verse.line: Why wander, mind? Rest. Not replaying the past, not scripting the future, I take what comes.
verse.translation: Why do you wander about in vain, mind? Rest somewhere. Whatever is to happen happens just as it will, and not otherwise. Not recalling the past, not planning the future, I enjoy the pleasures that come to me unlooked-for.
verse.why: Stop seeking approval and rehearsing outcomes; the calm you want is already inside.
verse.misuse: Not an argument against planning; it is for the worry loop once you have done your part.

prasang.title: Vairagyashatakam: Advice to the mind
prasang.summary: The poet talks to his own mind: why exhaust yourself pleasing others, why replay the past and script the future, why roam everywhere but within. 'So what?' asks what all our gains amount to.

verse.meaning: Bhartrihari speaks to his own mind. He asks why it wanders in vain. He tells it to rest. He says whatever must happen will happen exactly as it will, and not otherwise. He chooses not to recall the past or script the future. He takes what comes to him unlooked-for. The verse proposes that you stop rehearsing outcomes. The calm you want is already inside you, waiting for you to let go.

story.for_you: You have a real visa deadline, but you are also in an grove of your own making, replaying the night at two in the morning. You are asking the mind to find the truth, but you are also asking it to script the future.

script: You are terrified and wired, staring at the screen at two in the morning. The visa deadline is real, and the fear is real. But the messages you are replaying right now are not solving anything. They are only wearing you down.
Arjuna confesses the mind is as hard to hold as the wind; Krishna answers. Arjuna said to Krishna:
चञ्चलं हि मनः कृष्ण प्रमाथि बलवद्दृढम्, तस्याहं निग्रहं मन्ये वायोरिव सुदुष्करम्.
In plain words: The mind is restless, stormy, stubborn and strong. Holding it feels like holding the wind.

Krishna does not deny that the mind is hard to hold. He simply names it and points to a different way. The mind is not meant to be caged, but to be steadied through repeated, gentle effort. This is easier said than done, because you cannot force the thoughts to stop. But you can train the mind to rest, even when the outcome is still unknown.

Right now, the mind is trying to control the visa by staying awake. That is not working. Let the replaying rest. You do not need to solve it at two in the morning. Just let the thoughts pass like the wind.
Can you let the wind blow for just a little while?

depth.life: You are wired and terrified at two in the morning. You are checking the messages again. The visa deadline is real and the fear is real, but the replaying is not moving the work forward. It is only wearing you down.
depth.points: The mind is not a machine you can command. It is restless and stormy, and it will not stay still by force. The belief that staying awake and replaying will control the outcome is the trap. The mind must be trained, not fought.
depth.practice: Place your phone face down and turn away from the screen for one minute. Do not think about the messages.
depth.question: What would it feel like if you let the mind rest for just one minute?
